chunks: Abu Muhammad, Hasan ibn Hamza al-Alawi al-Hussaini, may Allah be pleased with him, told us, saying: Muhammad Omiduwar told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid al-Anbari, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

May Allah curse gold and silver. None loves them except for the one who is from their species. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, gold and silver? He, peace be upon him, said: It is not as you think. The gold is only the one who causes the religion to vanish, and silver is the one who overfills disbelief.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of cursing gold and silver in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the cursing of gold and silver is metaphorical, referring to the qualities of 'gold' as that which consumes or perishes the faith, and 'silver' as that which spreads or overflows with disbelief. This interpretation shifts the focus from material wealth to spiritual corruption, aligning with the Shia exegetical tradition that views these metals as symbols for specific types of people or actions that undermine religious integrity. The distinction highlights how materialism and hypocrisy can act as corrosive forces within the community of believers.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abu Muhammed, Hasan bin Hamza al-Alawi al-Hussaini, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed Omiduwar, from Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid al-Anbari, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Harun bin Kharija, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

May Allah curse gold and silver. None loves them except for the one who is from their species. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, gold and silver? He, peace be upon him, said: It is not as you think. The gold  is only the one who causes the religion to vanish, and silver  is the one who overfills  disbelief.
